<a id="CssomView"></a>

### CSSOM View

`CssomView` · `src/web.ts:121`

How a page brings an element into view: its top at the top of the view, smoothly or at once.

Source: W3C, CSSOM View Module: § 5 the ScrollIntoViewOptions dictionary and the ScrollBehavior enumeration · `https://www.w3.org/TR/cssom-view-1/#dictdef-scrollintoviewoptions`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | `start` | The element's top at the top of the view |
| `smooth` | `smooth` | Scrolls smoothly |
| `instant` | `auto` | Scrolls as the browser does by default: at once |

<a id="Http"></a>

### HTTP

`Http` · `src/web.ts:13`

The methods, statuses, headers and directives that a server answers with and a client sends.

Source: RFC 9110 (semantics), RFC 9111 (caching), RFC 9112 (connections), RFC 6750 (bearer tokens) · `https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `scheme` | `http` | The scheme of HTTP addresses (§ 4.2.1) |
| `ok` | `200` | The request succeeded |
| `noContent` | `204` | The request succeeded, and there is nothing to send back |
| `notFound` | `404` | The requested resource does not exist |
| `serverError` | `500` | The server failed |
| `unavailable` | `503` | The service cannot answer for now |
| `post` | `POST` | Method: asks the server to act |
| `contentType` | `content-type` | Header: the media type of the body |
| `cacheControl` | `cache-control` | Header: the caching directives |
| `connection` | `connection` | Header: the options of the connection |
| `authorization` | `authorization` | Header: the credentials of the caller |
| `bearer` | `"Bearer "` | The scheme of a token and its space, before the token (RFC 6750, § 2.1) |
| `noCache` | `no-cache` | Directive: revalidate before any reuse |
| `keepAlive` | `keep-alive` | Option: keep the connection open |

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [A published value is cited, not copied](product.md#CitedNotCopied)

### Media types

`MediaTypes` · `src/web.ts:40`

The types a server announces for what it sends, with their character set when it has one.

Source: IANA media types registry; RFC 6838; RFC 8259, § 11 (application/json); WHATWG HTML (text/event-stream) · `https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `html` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` | An HTML page in UTF-8 |
| `json` | `application/json` | A body written in JSON |
| `jsonUtf8` | `application/json; charset=utf-8` | The same, its encoding said: UTF-8 |
| `eventStream` | `text/event-stream` | A stream of events sent by the server |

<a id="ServerSentEvents"></a>

### Server-sent events

`ServerSentEvents` · `src/web.ts:76`

The shape of the messages of a stream that a server keeps open to a page, to tell it what changed.

Source: WHATWG HTML, § Server-sent events · `https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `eventField` | `"event: "` | The field that names the event |
| `dataField` | `"data: "` | The field that carries the data |
| `endOfLine` | `"\n"` | Ends the line of a field (a line feed) |
| `comment` | `": "` | A comment line, ignored by the browser |
| `endOfMessage` | `"\n\n"` | An empty line ends the message |

<a id="UiEvents"></a>

### UI events

`UiEvents` · `src/web.ts:95`

The events a page hears from the person, by the names the DOM gives them, and the keys that activate what has the focus.

Source: W3C, UI Events (§ 3.4 mouse events, § 3.3 focus events, § 3.6 keyboard events), Pointer Events (pointerdown), and the HTML Living Standard (input, change, DOMContentLoaded) · `https://www.w3.org/TR/uievents/`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `click` | `click` | The person activates an element: a click, a tap |
| `pointerdown` | `pointerdown` | A finger touches, a pen or a mouse button goes down: the moment of a tap, before it is released (Pointer Events) |
| `keydown` | `keydown` | A key goes down |
| `input` | `input` | The value of a field changes as the person types or picks |
| `change` | `change` | The person settles the value of a control: an option chosen |
| `over` | `mouseover` | The pointer enters an element |
| `out` | `mouseout` | The pointer leaves it |
| `focusIn` | `focusin` | An element receives the focus (it bubbles) |
| `focusOut` | `focusout` | It loses the focus (it bubbles) |
| `loaded` | `DOMContentLoaded` | The document is parsed: its elements are there (HTML § 8.4) |
| `loading` | `loading` | The ready state of a document still being parsed (HTML § 3.1.3) |
| `enter` | `Enter` | The key that activates what has the focus (UI Events KeyboardEvent key values § 3.3) |
| `space` | `" "` | The space bar, which activates a button too |

- Serves: [A published value is cited, not copied](product.md#CitedNotCopied)

### URI

`Uri` · `src/web.ts:57`

The parts of an address (a server's, the path of a request) and the relative references that link documents together.

Source: RFC 3986, § 3 Syntax components and § 4.2 Relative reference; RFC 6761 (localhost) · `https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schemeEnd` | `:` | Ends the scheme (§ 3.1) |
| `authority` | `//` | Opens the authority: the host and its port (§ 3.2) |
| `portSeparator` | `:` | Separates the host from its port (§ 3.2.3) |
| `pathSeparator` | `/` | Separates the segments of a path (§ 3.3) |
| `query` | `?` | Opens the query, after the path (§ 3.4) |
| `localhost` | `localhost` | The machine itself (RFC 6761, § 6.3) |

<a id="WebAudioApi"></a>

### Web Audio API

`WebAudioApi` · `src/web.ts:183`

The latency an audio context asks for: "playback", the longest, for sounds that need no precise timing, which leaves the audio output to the other sounds of the device and spares the battery.

Source: W3C, Web Audio API 1.1: § 1.2.4 AudioContextLatencyCategory · `https://www.w3.org/TR/webaudio-1.1/#enumdef-audiocontextlatencycategory`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `playback` | `playback` | Prioritise sustained playback without interruption over latency and power |
